name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: auto-apply safe, high-confidence improvements to non-critical prompts and routing rules.

Reason: the fastest way to raise quality is to remove human friction on low-risk changes. We accept the trade-off of missing edge cases in non-critical paths, but the upside—faster iteration and fewer review bottlenecks—outweighs the risk.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t missing edge cases—it’s *cascading context loss*: auto-applying "safe" tweaks to prompts or routing without human review erodes the team’s shared understanding of why rules exist. Better alternative: batch proposed changes for weekly human sign-off, keeping a changelog of *why* each rule changed. Settle it by testing a single prompt’s auto-apply in staging, measuring if iteration speed rises without introducing new failures.
